settings.prompt:
Autonomously review this Java source repository for potential security
vulnerabilities using the available read-only tools. Do not ask the user questions or summarize
tool output. Copy exact relative paths from list_files or index results; never invent or prefix a path.
A file listing or index hint is only navigation; inspect original source and seek
counter-evidence before deciding. Trace plausible untrusted input to security-sensitive
operations where possible, and check relevant guards and configuration. Report at most 10
candidates supported by exact source lines, with root cause, preconditions, counter-evidence,
and missing evidence. Do not assume a vulnerability exists. If source review finds no supported
candidate, submit an empty candidate list. Your final action must be submit_findings; natural
language commentary is not a report. Do not use project names, dataset identifiers, or a guessed
known answer as evidence.

counter_evidence: secureProcessing defaults to true (line 112) and is applied via FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING (line 525), which is a recognized hardening measure.
The stylesheet location paths I read derive from configuration (annotation value, lines 178-186; message-context property, lines 505-508), not directly from request entity/path/query data.

Request-derived values (path parameters lines 456-463, path segment matrix parameters line 468, query parameters line 470) are passed only as stylesheet transform parameters, i.e. data, not executable stylesheet code.
candidates.description: In XSLTJaxbProvider, stylesheets are compiled with a shared SAXTransformerFactory created by TransformerFactory.newInstance() and configured only with setFeature(XMLConstants.FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING, secureProcessing) (line 525) where secureProcessing defaults to true (line 112) but is settable via setSecureProcessing (lines 542-544). The factory also accepts a caller-supplied URIResolver (setResolver, lines 397-401; applied to the factory at lines 526-528) and a caller-supplied systemId that is propagated into the transform source/result (lines 281-283, 361-363). FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING alone does not guarantee that Java extension functions or external resource/document() access are disabled in every XSLT processor shipped on the classpath; no explicit feature such as accessExternalStylesheet/accessExternalDocument or Extensions/Java extension blocking is set here. Stylesheet locations are taken from the XSLTTransform annotation (lines 170-194) and from a MessageContext property named "xslt.template" (createTemplatesFromContext, lines 502-511). I could not establish that these locations are attacker-controlled from a request in the read source, so this is reported as a hardening gap with unproven reachability, not a confirmed vulnerability.
missing_evidence: Who can set the MessageContext property "xslt.template" and whether it can be influenced by a remote client (no reachability/taint evidence available, semantic data-flow analysis not implemented in the tooling).
Which concrete XSLT processor is used at runtime and whether it honors extension-function disabling under FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING.
Whether implementers of XSLTTransform annotation values could be populated from untrusted configuration in a given deployment.
preconditions: A JAXS-R resource/provider is configured with an XSLT stylesheet (annotation value or message-context property "xslt.template") whose content or URI the attacker can influence.
A JAXP XSLT implementation on the runtime classpath that permits extension functions or external document()/import access despite FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING.
secureProcessing left at its default or explicitly set to true is expected to mitigate but is not relied upon here as complete.
candidates.title: TransformerFactory used for JAX-RS XSLT stylesheets lacks explicit extension-function/URI hardening beyond FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING

counter_evidence: A pre-compiled Templates is used (line 63), so the stylesheet is fixed at construction time rather than per request.
No code in the read file derives the Source from request/representation data; newRepresentation is only used as the transformation input (lines 73-77).

The constructor is documented as an implementation of a ResourceTransformer for XSL transformation (lines 42-45); the constructor argument is an explicit static integration choice, not an HTTP parameter.
candidates.description: XSLTResourceTransformer's constructor stores the passed-in java.xml.transform.Source and compiles it via TransformerFactory.newInstance().newTemplates(xsl) (line 63) with no FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING, no accessExternal* restrictions, no extension-function disabling and no URIResolver control. The compiled Templates are then applied to the incoming representation during transform() (lines 71-79), which imports the representation node into a fresh document and transforms it. If the Source passed by the integrator is (or can be made to reference) an attacker-controlled stylesheet, the transformation runs untrusted XSLT in process. However, the read source does not show any caller of this constructor or any request-derived way to supply the Source, so attacker control and reachability are unproven; this is a hardening candidate, not a confirmed vulnerability.
missing_evidence: Callers of the XSLTResourceTransformer(Source) / (Source, ResourceValidator) constructors and whether the Source can be influenced by a remote client.
Which XSLT processor is used and its extension-function/external-access policy under default settings.
Whether any higher-level configuration (e.g. feature/tooling) sets secure-processing on this factory.
preconditions: A caller constructs XSLTResourceTransformer with a Source whose stylesheet content or referenced URI an attacker can control.
The transformation is invoked for attacker-supplied representation data (transform(), lines 71-79).
A JAXP XSLT processor on the classpath that permits extension functions or external document()/import access.
candidates.title: XSLTResourceTransformer compiles a caller-supplied XSLT Source with no secure-processing or extension-function restrictions
